title: Come, O Thou All-victorious Lord
description: Come, O Thou All-victorious Lord in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 84.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, O thou all vic-to-rious Lord! Thy power to us make known; Strike with the ham-mer of thy word, And break these hearts of stone.

lines: Thy power to us make known;
Strike with the hammer of thy word,
And break these hearts of stone.
O that we all might now begin
And turn at once from every sin,
Give us ourselves and thee to know,
Fill every soul with sacred grief,
The knowledge of our sickness give,
That blessed sense of guilt impart,
Trouble, and wash the troubled heart
Our desperate state through sin declare,
And take us up to heaven.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
